summary: Gradual 5xx rise during Dedicated GPU driver reset and prefetch replay
description:
Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13 14:10 UTC we observed a slow, stepwise rise in 5xx errors for a Dedicated customer (NimbleDocs) using pinned model rw-large-v1.1. Errors manifested as 502/504 from API Gateway with upstream runtime process restarts. Impact: customer-facing failures for batch embedding and streaming chat sessions, elevated error rate ~12% during peak.

Environment: prod (us-west-2), Dedicated GPU pool (pinned tenant), runtime version: rtx-serve-2.7.3, gpu-driver package: nvidia-530.11.

Observed behaviour: Initial symptoms were intermittent higher latency and sporadic 502s. Over ~30 minutes failures increased and stabilized at an elevated rate. Multiple runtime instances in the dedicated pool reported NVML reset events and kernel retries, followed by prefetch cancellations and hedged retry amplification at the API Gateway.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Replay customer workload (bulk embedding batch of ~50k small docs) against tenant with concurrency 60. 2) Trigger model prefetch by requesting a cold variant. 3) Observe incremental 5xxs and runtime NVML resets in logs.

Logs and metrics pointers: See apigw-error-rate dashboard (dashboard id: apigw-prod-usw2), runtime logs group: /var/log/runtime/dedicated/tenant-ndoc, NVML metrics exported to prometheus: nvml_gpu_driver_resets_total spikes aligned to error uptick.

Initial mitigation: temporarily reduced concurrency and disabled hedged retries for the tenant, which reduced error amplification but did not eliminate driver resets.
timeline: 2026-03-13T14:08Z - Alert: apigw 5xx rate alarm triggered for tenant NimbleDocs
2026-03-13T14:15Z - Support triage: assigned to infra-oncall (Marco Rivera); collected logs and created ticket
2026-03-13T14:30Z - Observed NVML reset spikes on 3/8 GPUs in dedicated pool
2026-03-13T15:05Z - Applied mitigation: reduced tenant concurrency from 60->20; disabled hedged retries
2026-03-13T15:25Z - Error rate dropped from 12% -> 3% but driver resets persisted intermittently
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: recent GPU driver (nvidia-530.11) introduced a firmware interaction causing corrected ECC events and soft resets under bursty prefetch.
Hypothesis B: runtime prefetch logic triggered pathological memory access pattern leading to page fault thrashing on affected GPU SKUs.
Logs show repeated 'nvmlDeviceReset' and 'GPU page fault' messages preceding runtime exit with signal 6.
Correlation observed between large embedding batches and NVML resets; smaller chat sessions unaffected when concurrency limited.
We reproduced driver reset locally on a spare node by running customer-style embedding batch while running model hot-swap; nvml logs identical.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) - 2026-03-13T14:20Z: Engaging infra-oncall due to NVML resets. Collected sample logs and heap profiles, attached to PRs.
Marco Rivera (Infra Oncall) - 2026-03-13T14:40Z: Noted firmware-corrected ECC warnings; isolating affected GPU host and removing from pool for repro.
Lina Cho (Serving Runtime) - 2026-03-13T15:10Z: Added debug flags to runtime to log prefetch memory map and KV cache operations. Observed prefetch cancellations concurrent with driver reset.
Support (Aisha) - 2026-03-13T15:30Z: Customer notified of temporary concurrency cap and told to expect reduced throughput; they confirm reduced failures but still see occasional errors.

Marco Rivera - 2026-03-13T16:00Z: Opened infra PR to pin older stable driver (nvidia-525.x) for struggling pool and scheduled rolling reboot of affected hosts. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/981
resolution_notes: Mitigation in progress: Removed affected hosts from Dedicated tenant pool and pinned customer's workload to unaffected hosts; rolled back GPU driver to 525.x on isolated repro hosts. Hedged retry and prefetch tuning applied as temporary controls. Awaiting confirmation from customer; long term fix requires coordinated firmware/driver update or runtime prefetch throttling.
